headline: Bluff Definition Activity — Balderdash-Style Vocabulary Game for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students engage deeply with new vocabulary by constructing plausible definitions, not just memorising them
Build critical reading skills by evaluating multiple definitions and identifying linguistic tells
Develop persuasive writing in English — a convincing bluff requires precise, confident language
Generate genuine motivation to learn word meanings when fooling classmates becomes the goal
howItWorks: The AI selects a challenging or unusual word from the lesson topic and keeps it secret from the class
Every student writes their own fake definition on their device — the more convincing, the better
The real definition is mixed in with the student bluffs and all definitions are displayed on screen
Students vote for what they believe is the real definition — scoring rewards both spotting the truth and fooling others
teacherUseCases: Vocabulary introduction — surface prior knowledge before teaching formal definitions
Academic word study — work with subject-specific or IELTS/TOEFL vocabulary lists
Creative writing warm-up — students practise writing with precision and authority in English

faq.q: What kind of words work best?
faq.a: Low-frequency vocabulary where students genuinely don't know the answer. Academic words, topic-specific terms, and unusual English idioms all work well. If students already know the word, the bluffing game collapses — the AI picks words calibrated to the difficulty level you set.

Students earn 1 point for submitting a definition and 1 point for voting for the real definition. They also earn 2 points for every classmate they fool — so a great bluff that tricks half the class is worth far more than just being correct.

faq.q: What if students write offensive or inappropriate definitions?
faq.a: The teacher sees all submitted definitions before the vote phase begins. You can remove any definition that isn't suitable before displaying them to the class — the game waits for you to approve the reveal.

faq.q: Can I set the target word myself?
faq.a: The AI generates words based on your topic and difficulty setting. If you want a specific word, set a very narrow topic (e.g. 'the word photosynthesis') and the AI will build the round around it.

faq.q: What proficiency level suits this activity?
faq.a: Bluff Definition works best from A2 upward. The writing task is low-stakes enough that beginners can attempt it, but the vocabulary challenge scales with difficulty — Advanced mode surfaces genuinely rare words that even strong students find tricky.

faq.q: Is Bluff Definition free to use?
faq.a: Yes, Bluff Definition is free. Students join on any phone or tablet through a browser link — no account or app download required.
